Exercise: Side Standing Long Jump

Category:
plyometrics

Exercise Type:
compound

Force Type:
push

Difficulty Level:
beginner

Movement Patterns:

- ankle_plantarflexion
- unilateral_hip_extension

Primary Muscles:

- quadriceps

Secondary Muscles:

- calves
- glutes
- hamstrings

Equipment:
None

Fatigue Score:
3

Systemic Fatigue:
low

Stimulus To Fatigue Ratio:
2.5

Energy Requirement:
high

Recovery Time:
48 hours

Goals:

- hypertrophy
- power_and_explosiveness

Contraindications:

- Recent lower body injury or surgery
- Severe joint pain or instability

Exercise Variations:

- name: Side Standing Long Jump with Medicine Ball Throw, id: Side_Standing_Long_Jump_Medicine_Ball_Throw

Substitution Options:

- name: Single-Leg Box Jump, id: Single_Leg_Box_Jump

Instructions:

- Begin standing with your feet hip width apart in an athletic stance. Your head and chest should be up, knees and hips slightly bent. This will be your starting position.
- Leaning to your right, extend through your hips, knees, and ankles to jump into the air. Block with the arms to lead the movement, jumping as far to your right as you can.
- Land facing the same direction with your feet hip width apart, absorbing the impact through your lower body.
